submission.justification: Module-D1 at 30% wall coverage achieves the highest possible light collection performance of 53.22 PE/MeV, maximizing the primary goal. This configuration outperforms Module-D3 by 43% (37.32 PE/MeV) and Module-D2 by 113% (24.95 PE/MeV) at the same coverage. The recommendation is based on comprehensive simulation data covering all three candidate designs across the full allowed coverage range (5-30%). The 30% coverage is optimal because it represents the maximum allowed limit and light collection scales sublinearly with coverage (~coverage^0.8). Module-D1's large-area light guide with bonded dichroic filter technology consistently demonstrated superior performance at every coverage level tested. CRITICAL CAVEAT: Thermal cycling reliability data (≤5% failure rate after 20 cycles, 300K to 87K) was not available in any project documents for any of the three designs. This recommendation assumes Module-D1 meets this hard constraint. If reliability testing reveals Module-D1 exceeds the 5% failure threshold, the recommendation should shift to Module-D3 at 30% coverage as the next-best alternative. Given that modules cannot be replaced once the cryostat is filled, verifying thermal cycling performance before deployment is essential.
